extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2024 reviewers (main track and position paper track)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for reviewers assessing main-track and position papers submitted to ICML 2024, including qualitative prompts, numerical ratings, overall scoring, and procedural requirements (e.g., Code of Conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer commitment is 'essential to the success of ICML.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected to honor the timeline and obligations; see accompanying blog post for additional context on review considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper summary (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions" without critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary of contributions only (explicitly requested to be without critique) to help area chairs and authors understand the reviewer’s perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate originality of the work (broad definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the ideas/results present new contributions relative to the research area; ICML uses broad definitions for originality—consider novelty of problem, approach, insights, or results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate quality of the work (broad definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge technical soundness, rigor of experiments/analysis, and correctness of claims; ICML frames 'quality' broadly to include methodological and empirical robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate clarity of the presentation (broad definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider writing quality, organization, and whether the paper communicates ideas and context effectively to its intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the significance of the paper for the research area (broad definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess impact, potential influence on the field, and whether the contributions advance understanding or practice in a meaningful way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions for authors (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pose questions that could 'change your opinion, clarify a confusion'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific, answerable questions that, if addressed by authors, might affect the review outcome or resolve uncertainties; prioritize queries that directly impact soundness or contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and societal impacts (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address whether limitations and societal impacts are 'adequately addressed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the paper acknowledges limitations and potential societal consequences, and whether mitigation or discussion is sufficient given the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag ethical concerns for specialized review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission raises ethical issues (e.g., potential misuse, harmful impacts, problematic data practices), mark these so the paper receives specialized ethical review as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness (numerical rating 1-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness: Technical validity of claims and methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate on a 1–4 scale the extent to which the paper's claims are supported by correct methods, analyses, and evidence; consider experimental design, proofs, and reproducibility aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (numerical rating 1-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation: Writing quality and contextual framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate on a 1–4 scale how well the paper is written, organized, and situated within related work; include clarity of figures/tables and accessibility of explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution (numerical rating 1-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contribution: Importance and originality for the research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate on a 1–4 scale the importance and novelty of the paper's contributions for its intended research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (1-10 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall assessment of the paper on a 1–10 scale (10 = Award quality ... 1 = Very Strong Reject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed descriptors across the scale: e.g., 10 = 'Award quality: Technically flawless paper', down through levels to 1 = 'Very Strong Reject'. Choose the overall score to reflect a combination of soundness, contribution, presentation, and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a 1–5 confidence rating to indicate how certain you are in your evaluation (higher means greater certainty based on expertise and evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position paper — clarity of stated position
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Position Paper Track: whether the paper 'clearly state[s] a position' on machine learning topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess if the paper articulates a clear stance or perspective; clarity of the position is central to evaluation in this track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position paper — support quality and numerical ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Position papers are evaluated via six numerical ratings examining support quality, plus an overall score using similar 1–10 scaling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate the evidence, arguments, and reasoning used to support the stated position across the provided rating dimensions (six numerical ratings are used by the review form); produce an overall 1–10 score analogous to main track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Both tracks require Code of Conduct acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must acknowledge and adhere to the conference Code of Conduct as part of the review process; failure to do so is a procedural violation.
